correctness.rationale: With \(d=b+c\) and \(u=kb/2\), \(v=kc/2\), each of the three published trigonometric factors reduces exactly under \(x=\tan u\), \(y=\tan v\) to a polynomial numerator over a positive denominator; their product is \(Q=(3-xy)(3-x^2-4xy)(3-y^2-4xy)\) divided by \((1+x^2)^2(1+y^2)^2\). For fixed \(x>0\), the four relevant \(y\)-roots have one and only one ordering transition, at \(x=\sqrt{3/5}\), established by evaluating the quadratic factor at \(r_B\). Sign alternation gives the allowed intervals. Irrational \(b/c\) gives torus equidistribution, whose tangent push-forward is the independent standard Cauchy law. Integrating the exact interval masses proves the displayed one-dimensional formula. The bundled verifier independently checks the algebra on a grid and reproduces the decimal value; finite computation is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The primary source identifies the incommensurate density as a universal spectral invariant but can only obtain it from a numerical two-dimensional area because the inequality appears analytically intractable. The new result resolves that concrete bottleneck: it exposes a simple cubic-factor sign geometry, proves the unique root-order transition, converts the two-dimensional area to a one-dimensional exact integral, and gives a reproducible high-precision value. This is a structural description of the source's universal constant rather than a routine extra digit or parameter substitution.
risks: The exact integral may or may not admit a further named closed form; the value assessment rests on resolving the source sign geometry, not on such a simplification.
